key_insight: Symmetry-preserving variational circuits accurately approximate lattice Gross–Neveu states, while adaptive circuits support transfer to larger systems without target-side reoptimization.
engineering_relevance: The adaptive construction offers linear precompilation local-factor growth with volume and a volume-independent shared-parameter count when flavor number, range caps, and append count are fixed.
method: Build fixed ansätze that conserve total fermion number or each flavor number.
Use SC-ADAPT-VQE with bulk, boundary-sensitive, and cross-flavor generators.
Prepare sector-resolved excited states by sequential deflation and assess degenerate eigenspaces using projector fidelities.
evidence_signal: Classical benchmarks reach 30 qubits; selected massive fixed ansätze achieve relative energy errors of approximately 10⁻⁵–2×10⁻⁴, while one-flavor circuits transferred to 60–400 qubits show 0.35%–1.76% deviations from DMRG references.
watch_item: Fixed-accuracy scaling to arbitrary volumes remains unestablished, and the large-system transfer results rely on matrix-product-state evaluation rather than quantum-hardware execution.
paper_title: Symmetry-Preserving and Scalable Variational Circuits for the Lattice Gross-Neveu Model
